news.title: Mizzou football announces home-and-home series with Cincinnati
news.lede: On Tuesday, Mizzou football announced a future two-game series with the University of Cincinnati, according to a release. Mizzou will host Cincinnati in Columbia on Sept. 18, 2027, and the Tigers will travel to the Bearcats in Cincinnati in 2032. Illinois canceled three upcoming games with Mizzou, including in 2027 and 2028, replacing them with a home-and-home series with Notre Dame. "As a result of Illinois' recent decision to cancel previously agreed-upon games, we moved quickly to secure a replacement opponent for 2027 that meets SEC and College Football Playoff scheduling requirements," Mizzou athletic director Laird Veatch said in a release.

news.title: Three uncapped players named in Football Ferns squad for Philippines matches
news.lede: This story was corrected on 18 November to say three new caps, not two. Three uncapped players have been named in the Football Ferns final squad of the year for a crucial two-match series against the Philippines ahead of next year's World Cup. The Football Ferns will face the world's 39th-ranked side at Porirua Park on 29 November and 4 December. It will be the side's last international fixtures ahead of the FIFA Women's World Cup 2027 draw in December.

news.title: Fern Rebekah Stott joins world football stars in FIFA social impact project
news.lede: Football Fern Rebekah Stott has been selected for a FIFA programme designed to help international footballers use their influence to create positive social change. Stott (33) is among 13 players chosen for the second intake of FIFA’s Player Impact Programme, which provides support and guidance to develop community initiatives. The nine-month programme aims to help players turn their ideas into projects addressing issues such as education, mental health and access to sport. Stott joins a group of international stars including Spain’s World Cup winner Alexia Putellas, Canadian captain Jessie Fleming and England forward Michelle Agyemang.

news.title: Spain’s Morocco Obsession: Why Has the 2030 World Cup Final Become a Political Battle?
news.lede: Rabat - Morocco is increasingly becoming a familiar name in Spain's domestic political debate, and football is not the only reason. With the 2030 FIFA World Cup approaching, Spanish politicians are repeatedly invoking the North African country in arguments about national prestige, political leadership, and Spain's position in the historic three-country hosting project. What was initially presented as a joint opportunity between Morocco, Spain, and Portugal is increasingly taking the shape of a political confrontation, with Morocco becoming a recurring reference in Spain's electoral messaging. The latest intervention came from Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of Spain's opposition People's Party (PP), who suggested that Spain should withdraw from organizing the tournament if FIFA awards the final to Morocco.
